turns.reply:
**Gut feel on architecture (Northwind Health – early Discover stage)**

For a classic three-tier .NET/IIS + claims app + Oracle Database workload moving from on-prem to OCI (us-chicago-1, HIPAA-driven), the natural fit is a **lift-and-modernize** pattern that keeps the Oracle DB as the anchor while modernizing the front tiers.

### High-level sketch
- **Database tier**: Oracle Autonomous Transaction Processing (ATP) or Exadata Cloud Service in us-chicago-1. This gives you native Oracle compatibility, automatic encryption at rest/transit, and built-in HIPAA controls (audit, key management via OCI Vault). Avoid self-managed DB VMs unless you have very specific licensing or tuning needs.
- **Application tier**: The claims-processing .NET app runs on **OCI Compute** (VM.Standard.E5 or E6 shapes) or, better, **OKE** (Kubernetes) with Windows/Linux node pools if you want containerization. Use OCI Load Balancer + WAF in front for traffic management and DDoS protection.
- **Web tier**: IIS front-end also on the same OKE/Compute footprint, fronted by the same LB. Keep session affinity if the app still relies on it.
- **Networking & security (HIPAA-critical)**: Single VCN with three private subnets (web, app, DB), bastion host or OCI Bastion service, private endpoints for DB, OCI IAM + MFA, encryption everywhere, and Object Storage + Vault for any audit logs or file uploads.
- **Observability & compliance**: OCI Logging + Monitoring + Audit service enabled by default; integrate with your existing SIEM if needed.

This keeps the Oracle DB as the “source of truth” (matching your confirmed facts) while giving the .NET layers a path to containers and autoscaling. It’s low-risk for an early-stage migration and directly addresses HIPAA audit/encryption requirements.
